claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments embedded in a Cu matrix.
Standard high-temperature sintering followed by slow cooling causes incipient phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
Standard high-temperature sintering followed by slow cooling causes interfacial voids in the W–Cu composite.
Rapid quenching immediately after high-temperature processing suppresses phase separation relative to conventional slow cooling.
Rapid quenching immediately after high-temperature processing suppresses interfacial void formation relative to conventional slow cooling.
Rapidly quenched W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity than slowly cooled W–Cu under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The proposed intervention is to water-quench or otherwise rapidly quench the W–Cu composite immediately after high-temperature processing instead of slow cooling.
The intervention should be applied near the onset temperature for phase separation.
Rapid quenching creates a kinetically trapped, metastable W–Cu interfacial region.
The metastable quenched interface has enhanced atomic bonding.
The metastable quenched interface has a reduced void density.
Rapid quenching limits atomic mobility and interfacial diffusion.
Limiting interfacial diffusion hinders the kinetics of phase separation and void coalescence.
Reduced phase separation and void coalescence preserve intimate W–Cu interfacial contact.
Preserved interfacial contact improves electron and phonon transport across the W–Cu boundary, including under irradiation.
Rapidly quenched W–Cu will have a lower interfacial void density than slowly cooled W–Cu.
Rapidly quenched W–Cu will have a more uniform phase distribution than slowly cooled W–Cu.
Interfacial void formation and phase separation degrade the thermal conductivity of slowly cooled W–Cu during service.
The benefit of quenching is expected to persist under moderate irradiation doses and high thermal flux typical of plasma-facing joints.
The long-term stability of the metastable interface under continuous irradiation and thermal cycling is uncertain.
